hints: Use the binomial theorem $(a+b)^5$ with $a = x^{-1}$ and $b = 3x^2$.
Determine the value of $r$ for which the power of $x$ is $1$.
walkthrough:
Write the general term in the binomial expansion of $\left(\frac{1}{x} + 3x^2\right)^5$:
$$T_{r+1} = \binom{5}{r} \left(x^{-1}\right)^{5-r} \left(3x^2\right)^r = \binom{5}{r} 3^r x^{-(5-r) + 2r} = \binom{5}{r} 3^r x^{3r - 5}$$

Set the power of $x$ equal to $1$ to find the index $r$:
$$3r - 5 = 1 \implies 3r = 6 \implies r = 2$$

Calculate the coefficient corresponding to $r = 2$:
$$\text{Coefficient of } x = \binom{5}{2} \times 3^2 = 10 \times 9 = 90$$
